overview: Black plays an Agincourt-style ...e6, ...a6 and ...c5, then 4.g3 b5, offering a queenside pawn to open lines against White's king and win time with ...Bb7. White can take with cxb5 axb5 Nxb5 and Black has a half-open a-file and an open diagonal. Reasoned from the moves; I do not know the theory well.

white_ideas.idea: Capture on b5 and develop Bg2 and O-O, keeping the extra pawn.
Maintain the centre with d4 or Nxb5 and Qa4 hits.

black_ideas.idea: Recapture axb5 and use the open a-file with ...Rxa2 ideas and ...Bb7 on the long diagonal.
Push ...c4 and ...Bb7 hitting the white king.

typical_structures.structure: Sicilian-like asymmetric centre with open a-file after cxb5 axb5.

character.notes: Black gives a pawn for open lines and development, so it is double-edged.

gambit.notes: Black's b5 pawn is offered with the open a-file and Bb7 as compensation, and White can keep it.

soundness.notes: Played by strong players such as Shabalov; compensation is believed to be enough, but I am unsure.

structure.notes: Sicilian-style asymmetric centre with an open a-file.

approach.notes: Seldom played even by strong players; chosen for surprise.

level.notes: Plans are subtle and move order is tricky.
